data.narrative:
Qilimanjaro is a Series A quantum computing company that has raised $10M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 quantum computing firms—3 public (IonQ, Rigetti Computing, D-Wave Quantum) and 8 private peers including Quantinuum, IonQ, and Infleqtion—though meaningful peer multiples at the Series A stage proved unavailable.

Stage-progression methodology is the applicable triangulation approach here. Using total capital raised ($10M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-subsequent-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $20M. This method reflects standardized venture-stage growth expectations absent company-specific margin or revenue data.

The peer-median approach was not applicable; while 6 same-sector comparables exist, insufficient overlap emerged within narrow filters (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation tier) to support a robust median. A cross-sector median would introduce unwarranted noise. Analysis therefore relies on the single stage-progression result. The triangulated range is $17M–$23M (low-median-high), anchored on the $20M point estimate. Key uncertainties include the absence of disclosed financials, revenue traction, or IP/patent valuation data, and the nascent state of quantum hardware commercialization generally, which limits predictive power of traditional venture multiples.
